As Fire Captain with the Orange County Fire Authority for 34 years, Joe lives and breathes public service – literally. He's spent his life putting the needs of our community ahead of his own.
When crisis struck Orange County during its 1994 bankruptcy, Joe saved countless jobs and livelihoods by creating the first Orange County firefighter union. He served as their President for 17 years, and while there, he balanced OCFA’s budgets, created a healthcare system for his firefighters, and increased their benefits.
As a labor leader, Joe helped get over 200 bills and initiatives passed and signed into law by five governors and two presidents. These bills and initiatives offered solutions to public safety, climate change, and policies to help working people.
Joe knows how hard it is for families to get ahead these days, and he knows what it takes to regrow the working class. As a decorated firefighter and labor leader, he has a record of delivering real results for working people. He will do the same for us in Washington. Can we count on you to donate to Joe’s campaign, so we can elect him to Congress to fight for us? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upliftjoekerr?refcode=X_062924_publicsafety]

Friend, I’m in the business of history. I have devoted decades of my life to making films that tell America’s stories and remind people of our vast and complicated past so we can better understand where our nation is – and, perhaps more importantly, where we are going.
From the Civil War to the Great Depression, from the global conflicts of the First and Second World Wars to the darkest days of the COVID-19 pandemic, these pivotal moments have tested our republic and forced us to reckon with the promise that defines the fabric of our nation – the responsibility to preserve a democratic system of government that respects the rights and addresses the needs of all of its citizens.
In November, our country faces another crossroads, and to me, this is a choice that could not be clearer. The democratic principles that have long been the bedrock of our nation are at risk, and the results of the November elections will have profound consequences for each of our futures.

body:
#
In the final days of our primary, conservative special interests dumped over $100,000 of dollars to try and defeat this progressive movement. Let us be clear:_It could have worked._
If we hadn’t been organizing from the very beginning, it might have done something. If we hadn’t been supporting our neighbors, we may have been vulnerable.
**But that special interest money didn’t work**.**Because money can’t buy a movement.** No poll-tested lines or flood of negative attacks on TV can overcome a group of people motivated by the desire to build a better world together.
Thanks to people like you – our volunteers, our fighters, our believers – we’ve made incredible progress on winning people on critical issues, on educating folks about challenges that affect our community, and on building a national progressive movement.
**But our work is not done.** We will not stop until we guarantee health care to every person, until we decarbonize our economy, until we end our system of mass incarceration and deportation, and until we finally win social, racial, economic, and environmental justice for all working people in this country.
**Our success so far has been powered by small-dollar donors chipping in an average donation of $17.25 at a time.** Tomorrow night at midnight, we’ll be facing our first FEC deadline since our movement won this primary, and now we’re gearing up to face a MAGA extremist on the ballot in November.
[**Can you make a donation in honor of our primary win to power this progressive movement and help us gear up for the attacks we’ll face from our MAGA challenger?**](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20240629.dPY7jv&refcode=em20240629-6731-P_FND_EOQ_GOL&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=6731%2E2526796%2ELYEbyk)
**[](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20240629.dPY7jv&refcode=em20240629-6731-P_FND_EOQ_GOL&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=6731%2E2526796%2ELYEbyk)**
**[Contribute $5](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20240629.dPY7jv&refcode=em20240629-6731-P_FND_EOQ_GOL&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=21&akid=6731%2E2526796%2ELYEbyk)**
**This is more than a moment**. It’s about who we are as people — working folks who try to hold the cause of justice at our cores. And if we work together, towards our common mission, there is nothing that we can’t do.
Pa'lante,
Team AOC

clean_body: In the final days of our primary, conservative special interests dumped over $100,000 of dollars to try and defeat this progressive movement. Let us be clear:It could have worked. If we hadn’t been organizing from the very beginning, it might have done something. If we hadn’t been supporting our neighbors, we may have been vulnerable. But that special interest money didn’t work.Because money can’t buy a movement. No poll-tested lines or flood of negative attacks on TV can overcome a group of people motivated by the desire to build a better world together. Thanks to people like you – our volunteers, our fighters, our believers – we’ve made incredible progress on winning people on critical issues, on educating folks about challenges that affect our community, and on building a national progressive movement. But our work is not done. We will not stop until we guarantee health care to every person, until we decarbonize our economy, until we end our system of mass incarceration and deportation, and until we finally win social, racial, economic, and environmental justice for all working people in this country. Our success so far has been powered by small-dollar donors chipping in an average donation of $17.25 at a time. Tomorrow night at midnight, we’ll be facing our first FEC deadline since our movement won this primary, and now we’re gearing up to face a MAGA extremist on the ballot in November. This is more than a moment. It’s about who we are as people — working folks who try to hold the cause of justice at our cores. And if we work together, towards our common mission, there is nothing that we can’t do. Pa'lante, Team AOC | ---|--- | | ---|---|--- Email us: mailto: speak@ocasiocortez.com

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: A leap of faith
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
Every contribution represents how when we link arms, we make each other stronger.

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=2252%2E4032634%2EQdi_qd)
---
I am grateful all the way down to my toes every time someone decides to donate any amount of money to this campaign. You know, the way I see it, if someone contributes $3, it’s a leap of faith. They may know that if they’re the only ones donating, their $3 won’t go too far. It might only be a drop in a bucket against all the funding from national Republicans and powerful interests. But that donor knows in their bones that they are not alone. They know they’re a part of a team — this team — of people across the country who believe that big, structural change is possible. It’s how we’ve been able to get student debt cancellation onto the President’s desk and started to make big freeloading corporations finally pay federal income taxes. Just this morning, someone from Florida made a $5 contribution, and someone else from Oklahoma made a $3 contribution. They did go out on a limb for what they believe in. And they are counting on people like you to match or exceed their contribution. To magnify their impact. To add up to a powerful grassroots movement and ensure universal child care, pass a wealth tax, and break up big monopolies overcharging consumers. [**If it makes sense for you right now, will you meet them out on that limb and make a donation of any amount before tomorrow night’s big FEC fundraising deadline? Every contribution — no matter the amount — will show the breadth and depth of this movement, and they will all add up to make real change.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/2273?t=8&akid=2252%2E4032634%2EQdi_qd)

I’m not kidding myself: the other side has big heaps of money. Giant corporations hire armies of lobbyists to get their way in Washington, and corporate PACs write big campaign checks to elect candidates who ask “How high?” when CEOs say “Jump.” But I’m fighting back against their model of business-as-usual. We’re building a different model — where grassroots donors fund grassroots campaigns that elect candidates who put our government on the side of families, not just the rich and powerful. This is about who our government works for. In fact, it’s about whether our democracy _works_ , period. And it starts every time someone believes that better is possible, takes a leap of faith, and invests in something that will benefit everyone in our country. [**So what do you say? Can you make a donation of $28 or any amount? Every contribution represents how when we link arms, we make each other stronger.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/2273?amount=28&t=14&akid=2252%2E4032634%2EQdi_qd) Thanks for being a part of this, Elizabeth

subject: A tough decision
body:
This is why I need your help.

Peter —
I had to make a tough decision today.
We had a meeting where we had to decide what our budget should be for digital ads this summer. A brand new poll showed us down by 1 point, so we know that we have to start reaching voters ASAP.
While I’d like to green-light the budget, I’m nervous because we’re so far off from our big end-of-quarter fundraising goal.
**So, I had to make a difficult call:** Should I move forward with a new investment in digital ads or wait to see if we hit our fundraising deadline goal?
Ultimately, I decided we should remain dark on ads and wait until we hit our fundraising goal. I hate this because it gives Republicans the upper hand. BUT if we see a surge in donations we can reach our goal and I’ll be able to give my team the green light ASAP.
Will you step up here, Peter? I really want to get these ads up, but I need your help. I’m dropping a custom ActBlue link below so I can track all our supporters who help us meet this goal.

Peter,
Tuesday was the 11-year anniversary of the Supreme Court’s disastrous decision in _Shelby County,_ which nullified Section 5 of the Voting Rights Act, taking away key protections and making it easier for states to make voting harder — particularly for people of color.
Since that ruling, far-right fanatics have followed the Roberts Court’s lead, bringing case after case to try to further degrade voting rights and damage our democracy.
But this week isn’t just a chance to reflect, it’s a timely opportunity to fight back. All On The Line’s quarterly fundraising deadline is coming up in less than 36 hours. **This anniversary is an important reminder that our democracy is fragile and we each need to do our part to strengthen it.**

clean_body: Democracy is fragile, and it’s counting on you. | = Peter, Tuesday was the 11-year anniversary of the Supreme Court’s disastrous decision in Shelby County, which nullified Section 5 of the Voting Rights Act, taking away key protections and making it easier for states to make voting harder — particularly for people of color. Since that ruling, far-right fanatics have followed the Roberts Court’s lead, bringing case after case to try to further degrade voting rights and damage our democracy. But this week isn’t just a chance to reflect, it’s a timely opportunity to fight back. All On The Line’s quarterly fundraising deadline is coming up in less than 36 hours. This anniversary is an important reminder that our democracy is fragile and we each need to do our part to strengthen it. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: = | = = | = = | = This important fundraising period for All On The Line comes as we close out another distressing term for the Supreme Court. You know, it’s hard to believe that it was 50 years ago this month when I saw the Supreme Court building for the first time. I was interning for the NAACP Legal Defense and Educational Fund and had to file a brief with the Court. I still remember what it was like to climb those marble steps and the awe I felt as I looked across the street at the Capitol. I’ve had a reverence for the judicial branch ever since. But since then, I’ve seen that we can’t depend on the courts to secure our democracy. That work falls to us. And we can’t let up now. = Eric H. name: Sara Jacobs
subject: The most impactful thing you can do in the 2024 elections
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Sara Jacobs for Congress
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em]
Since I’ve been involved in politics, and especially since I was elected to Congress, I get a lot of questions from friends and family about how they can most effectively impact the outcome of elections. People want to know the best way to help – and the good news is that the answer is pretty simple.
One of the absolute most impactful things you can do to ensure the outcomes we want in the 2024 elections (aside from voting!) is to donate to candidates you believe in.
Not everyone likes that answer. I get it – after reading headline after headline, seeing all the polls, and watching the news every night, we want to DO something. And at this exact moment in the election cycle, your donations have a seriously outsized impact on how things go, because they allow campaigns to scale up outreach, place targeted ad buys that directly reach the most critical undecided voters, and execute plans they’ve been mapping out for months and months.

Peter, If you saw Anastasia's message earlier this week, you know that we just launched our first TV ad of the campaign. **I want to talk to you about it for a second because it's a great example of why fundraising deadlines (like the one we have tomorrow at midnight) are so important.** Believe it or not, TV ads are still one of the most important ways we can get our message out to voters. Even when I grew up and ran for Congress, I was a Gen Z working class kid – I didn’t have the same advantages that other candidates have. As we embark on the Summer holidays and sit in traffic (during the normal work week), Blame Jim Himes. When you run a business and have to travel between clients and customers and have add an extra hour for leeway - Blame Jim Himes.
I will write more about this, but this speech I recently gave sums up Jim - No improvements for I-95 in 16 Years. Simple short-term solutions like moveable barriers will help especially in Stamford and Norwalk.
I will let the video speak today and hope you are all having a great weekend. But if you are stuck in traffic - Blame Jim Himes
Vote for me on August 13th with Early Voting August 5-11 and I will work to improve I-95.

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/87882340/482551937/2130526953?refcode=emwrapper&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZDk3YTM4OWEtNDEzNi1lZjExLTg2ZDItNjA0NWJkZDllMDk2IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=K1_FAX_IzXCHmkeC-p5EWwL-NAUbmBScAF7OTE69-9A=&emci=d47a389a-4136-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&emdi=d97a389a-4136-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&ceid=14016711)
Peter,
While media coverage has intensely focused on Joe Biden coming out of Thursday’s debate, less is being said about _CNN_ and the disastrous format that allowed Donald Trump to lie for nearly two hours straight without a single fact check from the moderators.
[**We’ll talk about how _CNN_ ’s disastrous debate performance was a huge gift to Trump in a moment, but if you’re ready to support COURIER’s mission to fact-check Trump and stop right-wing misinformation, can you chip in $20 now?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/87882341/482551948/-593472309?refcode=20240629-EM-DebateFollowUp&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZDk3YTM4OWEtNDEzNi1lZjExLTg2ZDItNjA0NWJkZDllMDk2IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=K1_FAX_IzXCHmkeC-p5EWwL-NAUbmBScAF7OTE69-9A=)
_CNN_ has infamously struggled with how to cover Trump. In 2016 they allowed him unfettered access to the network’s primetime shows while airing his hate and misinformation-filled rallies nonstop to pump up ratings. After Trump won, _CNN_ promised change, but there’s little evidence that they’ve learned anything at all.
_**Here’s what we mean:**_
**First,** problems started with a _CNN_ “town hall” during the Republican primary. Trump refused to debate his Republican opponents so _CNN_ offered him a one-on-one interview with politics anchor Kaitlin Collins. The “town hall” was widely criticized for Collins’ lack of fact-checking and the partisan audience that cheered Trump’s every word, including a standing ovation when he took the stage.
**Then,** during Trump’s New York election fraud trial, _CNN_ aired wall-to-wall coverage, including ridiculous live shots of Trump’s motorcade as it meandered slowly through rush hour traffic to the Manhattan courthouse.
**Now,** after becoming the first media organization to run a presidential debate in nearly 40 years, _CNN_ decided not to fact-check during the debate. The format was an especially insane decision because _CNN_ ’s own fact-checking team clocked Trump lying once every three minutes at a recent Wisconsin campaign rally.
**Predictably, Trump lied throughout the debate, and most talking heads in the press are saying he “won” handily (whatever that means).**
The easiest explanation for _CNN_ 's disastrous decision is that to avoid criticism that they were too hard on Trump, they took an outdated “both sides” approach to debate moderation.
By now we know that, when it comes to stopping Donald Trump from spreading lies and conspiracies, that approach isn’t good enough. In fact, it’s dangerous because it normalizes Trump’s anti-democratic candidacy and everything it represents.
Here at COURIER, we’re not afraid to say the truth: Trump is a liar and a fascist, and to protect our democracy, he must be held accountable.
**_CNN_ and the rest of the legacy media might pretend that Trump is “normal,” but we never will. **
**Right now, COURIER’s talented network of journalists in battleground states across the country is working hard to fact-check the lies and make our vital local election coverage freely available to the communities that need it most. **

In 2016 they allowed him unfettered access to the network’s primetime shows while airing his hate and misinformation-filled rallies nonstop to pump up ratings. After Trump won, CNN promised change, but there’s little evidence that they’ve learned anything at all. Here’s what we mean: First, problems started with a CNN “town hall” during the Republican primary. Trump refused to debate his Republican opponents so CNN offered him a one-on-one interview with politics anchor Kaitlin Collins. The “town hall” was widely criticized for Collins’ lack of fact-checking and the partisan audience that cheered Trump’s every word, including a standing ovation when he took the stage. Then, during Trump’s New York election fraud trial, CNN aired wall-to-wall coverage, including ridiculous live shots of Trump’s motorcade as it meandered slowly through rush hour traffic to the Manhattan courthouse. Now, after becoming the first media organization to run a presidential debate in nearly 40 years, CNN decided not to fact-check during the debate. The format was an especially insane decision because CNN ’s own fact-checking team clocked Trump lying once every three minutes at a recent Wisconsin campaign rally. Predictably, Trump lied throughout the debate, and most talking heads in the press are saying he “won” handily (whatever that means). The easiest explanation for CNN 's disastrous decision is that to avoid criticism that they were too hard on Trump, they took an outdated “both sides” approach to debate moderation. | | Peter, it’s Kirsten. I’m sure your inbox is full of emails right now from people asking for money. I hate to add to it, but our campaign has a critical fundraising deadline coming up — and hitting our goal is non-negotiable. **Tomorrow night, our campaign legally has to turn in our fundraising numbers and make them public. This means everyone, from our supporters to our opponents, will know how much we have in the bank going into the final stretch of this race.** We’re already a target for BIG Republican spending. And depending on what these reports show, corporations and far-right groups will pour even more cash into my opponent’s pocket to help him win. When I lost by a percentage point in 2022, our campaign had been outspent 6:1. **I know we can take on outside spending — but I can only do it with your grassroots support.** Peter, in Congress, I’ll fight to protect a woman’s right to choose, bring good-paying jobs to Arizona, defend our access to water, make healthcare affordable for everyone, and more. Every single piece of legislation they've drafted, approved, and forced on WE, THE PEOPLE, has been a disaster. We had it good under President Trump. Our border was secure, inflation was down, and the American economy was BOOMING. Now, we're watching as Washington sends this country on a Kamikaze mission toward total destruction. It's now or never to step up and make a difference, Fellow American. body:
Aphasia may make it harder for me to speak. But I have not lost my voice.
#

Friends -
Thirteen years ago, a gunman shot me in the head while I was meeting with constituents in front of a grocery store in Tucson.
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-june24.gd3XnS&refcode=em240629-2-60&t=1&akid=8402%2E3935704%2EtwqDrN)
Because of the damage the bullet caused to the left hemisphere of my brain, where the language function sits, I have aphasia. This means that even though the words are in my head, I have a hard time getting them out.
**Aphasia may make it harder for me to speak. But I have not lost my voice.**
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-june24.gd3XnS&refcode=em240629-2-60&t=2&akid=8402%2E3935704%2EtwqDrN)
The road to recovery hasn’t been easy for me, but I’ve never given up. In addition to speech therapy and physical therapy, I dedicate much of my time to riding my bike, playing my French horn, and practicing yoga. These activities have helped me so much in my recovery journey.
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-june24.gd3XnS&refcode=em240629-2-60&t=3&akid=8402%2E3935704%2EtwqDrN)
I know sometimes the challenge of ending gun violence in our nation can feel overwhelming. When we see the headlines after a mass shooting—or when we remember the countless tragedies that don’t make the news every day—I know how hard it can be.
But friends, we can’t give up. I have found my recovery journey and the fight to end gun violence to be very similar. Even on the hardest days, we can never lose hope.
Tomorrow, GIFFORDS PAC is facing its June FEC fundraising deadline. Our quarterly fundraising deadlines are a critical test for the gun safety movement, as both adversaries and allies will be looking to see if we have the resources to take on the gun lobby and elect gun safety champions this November.

The son of hardworking farmworkers, Dr. Ruiz grew up in Coachella, CA and learned at an early age that the key to attaining the American Dream is hard work and a great education. In the summer of 1990, Raul walked in the desert heat from business to business in the Coachella Valley asking them to invest in their community by contributing to his education. Let me tell you a little bit about myself.... I'm a retired Navy CAPT who spent 25 years fighting for our country in some of the most dangerous battlegrounds in the world. My family and I came to America when I was just four years old after my father was put on a kill list in Communist Vietnam. If it wasn't for America, I probably wouldn't be alive today. I owe my life to this country - so I paid her back by attending the Naval Academy after graduating high school and dedicating my career to serving America. I served in Iraq, Afghanistan, and Somalia where I defused IEDs for our SEAL teams and Special Forces. I performed some of the most dangerous dives in the military all around the world. It wasn't easy, and there were many times where my life flashed before my eyes. But it was worth it, because I was protecting this country so the next generation could have the same opportunities that I did. Now that Democrats are trying to destroy that American Dream, I'm not about to sit by idly. Our fight isn't just overseas anymore. It's right here in America, where far-Left liberals in Washington DC are working to erode your freedom and compromise our future. I'm not a career politician. I spent my life serving our country, not serving special interests. _**[But one thing about me is I've always been called to service, and that's why I'm running for U.S. Senate in Virginia.](http://links.primaryupdate.com/u/click?_t=e3c9a4cac7f248a39c2a3d920479a441&_m=bc7b3247ba5c474b9d6c3fc7d86f3555&_e=kfPG0Q56UQTtNXZ_1FwivYs9gtR9pD2bcDNQPWOOk8f-Zt84JupfHqTT2hHapjYySXX4rkt8-s6EgeXIU94D8pHDJ8S8ztD5Mryy68qLPkxFxoiTyrv7kaH5ejsX8FS_4XXGUH5bMfrh5PjXyV3aZdsC5S_1wSi9oc-n87urBk1Wb9V-IKspNeeO0zszh-kZH_J-iptVWcvSVO8lWtyNUoz1M4YQJnDYsOnhm9_i1fPVDqosH9Vo9_i3NzZZ-qrAPsq6ij-Ezdr3zo-gUjzJeA%3D%3D)**_

Wade_ and upended decades of precedent, allowing states like Idaho to implement draconian abortion bans — only adding more confusion and anxiety for doctors and patients seeking urgent, lifesaving reproductive care.

* Then, the Court overturned the so-called _Chevron_ doctrine — a key legal ruling that allows government agencies like the EPA to do their jobs. In one fell swoop, the Court showed its naked willingness to bend to corporate interests and give even more power to federal judges to overrule experts in all areas of government and policy. It is a disaster for our planet and our future.

Peter, for each of these reasons and more, I am relentlessly working to rein in this radical Supreme Court majority by passing urgent reforms and transparency measures. Derek,
This quarter, Congresswoman Katie Porter has introduced a whopping 6 pieces of legislation aimed at increasing transparency in government, earning the American people’s trust, and more!
Here’s a round-up of that legislation Katie introduced:
1) The _Legislative Proxy and Absence Accommodation Resolution_ will allow Members to once again vote by proxy in the case of illness or another unavoidable absence, keeping Congress running and giving Americans the representation we deserve.
2) The _Majority Rule Resolution_ ends the filibuster, which has prevented Congress from passing legislation that is broadly popular with a majority of the American people.
3) The _Congressional Bipartisan Seating Resolution_ would set in stone a bipartisan recommendation to alternate seating of Members’ party affiliation during committee hearings. This will foster a more collaborative working environment between both parties.
4) The _Lobbying Disclosure Modernization Act_ would finally consolidate information about who is lobbying in Congress into one accessible platform for public viewing. This would increase transparency and trust.
5) The _Block the Revolving Door Act_ would institute a two-year ban on lobbying for former Members of Congress and other high-level government employees.
6) The _Presidential Ethics Reform Act_ would require presidents and vice presidents to publicly disclose their tax returns. Voters have a right to know where their future leaders have been getting their money — and from whom.
Katie is focused on the future of our country, because she’s seen how desperately we need to enact real change.
Too many politicians are beholden to corporate PAC and lobbyist money and a system of legalized corruption. Our housing crisis, climate change, and rising prices are a direct result of this system, which puts corporate profits ahead of people.

\-- **Then,** I pointed out to MTG and her Republican allies that it’s flatly against the rules to make inappropriate comments about a fellow member of Congress.

\-- **Nevertheless,** she refused to apologize, and the Republican committee chairman even ruled that her behavior was fine.

**\--So I had no choice but to ask for clarification because I wanted to know if I could return the favor and discuss MTG’s appearance, too.**

This is what happens when people who don’t give a damn about the rules somehow end up in CONGRESS!

The only way to make sure MTG is held accountable for her outrageous attacks on me and my colleagues is by making sure her Republican allies never hold the House Majority again.

That’s why I’m reaching out to you personally.

Let me tell you the story of how “bleach-blonde, bad-built, butch body” was born: \-- First, Marjorie Taylor Greene insulted my appearance in an official House committee proceeding. \-- Then, I pointed out to MTG and her Republican allies that it’s flatly against the rules to make inappropriate comments about a fellow member of Congress. \-- Nevertheless, she refused to apologize, and the Republican committee chairman even ruled that her behavior was fine. \--So I had no choice but to ask for clarification because I wanted to know if I could return the favor and discuss MTG’s appearance, too. This is what happens when people who don’t give a damn about the rules somehow end up in CONGRESS! The only way to make sure MTG is held accountable for her outrageous attacks on me and my colleagues is by making sure her Republican allies never hold the House Majority again. We can’t rest up
| **Team —**

Here’s two things I know:

The old Republican Party is dead and gone.

The MAGA anarchists now in charge of the GOP are pushing a dangerous agenda as they chip away at our democracy.

**Don’t be fooled by their fake denials:**

They _do_ want to defund the FBI and fund the abortion police.

They _do_ want the courts to intervene and save Trump.

And they _do_ want to pass a nationwide abortion ban _without exceptions_ for rape, incest, or the life of the mother.

MAGA Republicans are counting on Democrats like you and me giving up — allowing Trump to stroll back into the White House while they keep the House, seize the Senate, and stack the courts. They are trying to overwhelm us with their money and anti-democratic tactics.

**That’s why we can’t stop fighting. If anything, it’s time to ramp up our efforts to make Republicans pay for their assault on our democracy.**

[Team — I need your help today. Voter Protection Project and I are committed to doing whatever it takes to end this dangerous MAGA threat. Before you move on to your next email--I would appreciate it if you would take a few moments to participate in Hillsdale College's **National Survey on the Department of Justice.**

The survey has only eight questions, and its subject affects your liberty and the very survival of the rule of law in America.

**The current administration 's weaponization of the Department of Justice is unprecedented in American history.**

Instead of protecting your God-given constitutional rights, the administration uses the Department of Justice to attack its political opponents...

...as well as Christians, parents, and anyone who dares to stand up for our constitutional liberties.

At the same time, with the help of the media it...

* Covers up a two-tiered justice system that violates your constitutional rights
* Hides the corruption of the ruling class
* Attacks those with traditional viewpoints

**That 's why I'm asking you to take the Hillsdale College National Survey on the Department of Justice.**

By completing this survey, you will help us more clearly understand the views of mainstream Americans like you on this critical issue. Your responses will help Hillsdale strengthen its nationwide educational outreach efforts on behalf of liberty--including the importance of the rule of law and checks and balances, which the American Founders saw as essential safeguards against corruption.

Friend, you can complete the National Survey on the Department of Justice by using the link below:

**[https://lp.hillsdale.edu/department-of-justice-survey/](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/u/click?_t=5b1853ae48754bee8f471363fe4933a9&_m=2a44c6a1e9564c1d94052892ad0a4059&_e=h3EfgZXKM5o8IChsdtWfMVtQQaSXj2YVbzru9HaEPe90QiOlopPBh5n1KM6roVdnryUVtEcxplljmhWzHJBsTc8gYDcKixtV9aZ26aCSckQs-Zn2PsUS2SN7XU8G1VkOwrpabrSSyx7F2HquupX00Ju7vaQi2Fovt7hapj_S6CsVoMZnlcX7gMEZsy7jgEV1S3l-MFguNeYhUm_qL5yrR6IoE8cvRKYtAV_kDCbLWlj87qGkOAPGY7WutJyZJBaILezqrDC5J2HpVppfo7Nc5Qgq2Ggst7zmxmp5kfoM7omrSCySq19sL1-bcuxwjplm11mMl4atgi7hM_9PdWLUbtGo0mlgWqz65Xbb0SpRvVhc4K2gZ9-YJSdrejzh95U8EYhFTRdwbhsd2c-MSwSmXA%3D%3D)**

The **Declaration of Independence** argues that **the purpose of just government is to secure our natural rights** and that **just government is founded on the consent of the governed.**

Yet today's ruling class regularly disregards the will of the American people, and our rights--to the freedoms of speech, assembly, and religion, to due process, to gun ownership, and more--are under constant attack.

**You and I know that liberty in America is under serious threat. But as I travel around the country, I tell the audiences I speak to how we are engaging in the fight against this threat.**

A vital part of our efforts in this fight--in which Hillsdale College is a leader--is **reaching** and **teaching** millions of citizens, with the TRUTH about America's great heritage of liberty.

We are heavily invested in our educational outreach efforts through our **Project to Defend Liberty Nationwide by Reaching and Teaching Millions.**

These efforts include:

* **Teaching bright and principled students** --on our campuses in Hillsdale, Michigan, and Washington, D.C.--who receive a rigorous, **classical liberal arts education, including** a required course on the Constitution
* **Distributing _Imprimis_** , America's leading digest of liberty, which is mailed to more than 6.4 million homes and businesses ten times per year; previous issues include "The Politicization of the Department of Justice" by Harmeet K. Dhillon
* **Producing and promoting free online courses** for any citizen who wishes to learn, on topics such as the Constitution, American history, and free market economics
* **Providing a classical K-12 curriculum** with a solid grounding in American history, constitutional government, and economics to schools that educate thousands of students nationwide

After everything we've seen over the past few years, the need for Hillsdale's educational outreach efforts is undeniable.

So please share your views by completing our **National Survey on the Department of Justice** and returning it to me as soon as possible. It only has eight questions and will take a few minutes of your time.

Your completed survey will help us form the most effective strategy to **reach** and **teach** millions of Americans on behalf of liberty.

**This independence frees the College from burdensome and corrupting government regulations. But it also means that our work depends entirely on the generous support of private citizens, like you, who understand the importance of education to liberty.**

Thank you for your time and attention. I look forward to receiving your completed survey, and I sincerely appreciate your support of Hillsdale's educational outreach efforts on behalf of liberty.

Warm regards,

Larry P. Arnn

Our new book, _The Perilous Fight_ , addresses these issues head-on, offering practical insights and solutions to restore and strengthen the family unit.

Why is this important? Because the family's pivotal role in our society is under threat, and without addressing these challenges, our foundational values may be lost. subject: Shattering expectations

body:
Peter: Gen Z will outlive the NRA. The Daily Beast recently analyzed the NRA’s tax returns. They aren’t pretty.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20240629-2&t=1&akid=869%2E587540%2EjmbZmN)
Mark my words, Peter: **Gen Z will outlive the NRA.**
_The Daily Beast_ analyzed the NRA’s tax returns a few months ago. They aren’t pretty.
In fact, the pro-gun group’s revenue has been on the decline for years now, especially since Parkland. _Last year, their fundraising was at its lowest point since 2008. And since 2018 they have lost over 1 million members._
I firmly believe that the NRA’s days are numbered—and as their power and influence fade into the dustbin of history, we will replace their corrupt, purchased politicians with a new generation of bold, courageous leaders who aren’t afraid to take urgent, necessary action to stop the scourge of gun violence in America.
**I co-founded Leaders We Deserve because Gen Z’s answer to the NRA is electing more and more young people to public office to counter their agenda.**
**[With so much riding on the upcoming elections, we’re preparing now so we can elect all 12 of our endorsed candidates on Election Day. Will you rush a $5 contribution now to help us meet our end-of-quarter fundraising goal and elect the leaders we deserve this November?](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lwd-em-20240629-2?refcode=em20240629-2&amount=5&refcode2=869_587540_jmbZmN&akid=869%2E587540%2EjmbZmN)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lwd-em-20240629-2?amount=5&refcode=em20240629-2-869&refcode2=869_587540_jmbZmN&akid=869%2E587540%2EjmbZmN)**
We founded Leaders We Deserve last year to elect the next generation of leadership—and folks across the country are already helping us shatter expectations.
Not only have tens of thousands of people just like you joined our movement and helped spread the word about our mission, we’ve already elected two candidates since we started.
In the days leading up to last November’s election, we hit the streets in Virginia to knock on doors and get out the vote for **Nadarius Clark**. Thanks to our supporters’ donations, we were proud to invest more than $100,000 to support Nadarius’s campaign.
When all the ballots were counted, _Nadarius won by less than 2,000 votes._
And just a few weeks ago, we were proud to help **Molly Cook** win a special election to become the youngest and first-ever LGBTQ+ member of the Texas Senate. We’re going to make sure she wins a full term this November!
Leaders We Deserve is already playing an integral role in electing the next generation of leaders and we’re counting on your continued support so we can keep winning these fights in 2024. **There is too much on the line for us to lose.**
**[Leaders We Deserve can only be successful in November with your continued support, so can you rush a $5 contribution to help us meet our end-of-quarter goal today? Anything you can give will make a difference.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lwd-em-20240629-2?refcode=em20240629-2&amount=5&refcode2=869_587540_jmbZmN&akid=869%2E587540%2EjmbZmN)**

Thank you for your consideration,
David Hogg

Peter,

The corrupt, rogue, increasingly illegitimate Supreme Court continues to churn out rulings that spell disaster for our personal freedoms, basic human rights, and a functioning democracy.

**Before I break down these latest rulings, I need your help:

[We have an urgent fundraising shortfall of $100K that we must close before the end of this month. Can you make a donation of $25, $50, $100 or more right now?](https://www.jillstein2024.com/donate?e=e813143e1dc0d3b0ffcb007ffe357333&utm_source=jillsteinforpresident&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=scotus_rulings&n=2)**

---
Yesterday two new rulings were handed down. The first, _Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo_ , thoroughly revoked the Chevron doctrine – which has been the backbone of every major federal regulation for 40 years.

This precedent has protected our air and water, workplace safety, labor rights, food and drug safety (just to name a few) from interference by uninformed, partisan lawmakers or lobbyists.

Revoking this rule essentially means that _only the court_ has the proper authority to determine whether or not a manufacturing plant is dumping too many cancer-causing chemicals into our water supply – not the scientists or doctors who study these things.

Ironically (or not), the Chevron doctrine was established in 1984 when a certain EPA Administrator in the Reagan administration was trying to thwart the EPA’s authority from the inside.

**That administrator’s name was Anne Gorsuch – mother of current Supreme Court justice Neil Gorsuch.

** Gorsuch was also front and center in the second ruling yesterday, _Grants Pass v. Johnson_ , which hardened our nation’s war on unhoused people by criminalizing sleeping – a basic human function essential to survival – in public.

**There are policy solutions to undo the damage caused by both of these rulings, and we must pursue those for immediate relief. But we**** _will_****find ourselves right back here if we take no action to rein in this court.

** The Supreme Court of the United States now sits at the top of a rogue and corrupt federal judiciary captured by fascists.

**[I have a plan to address this](https://www.jillstein2024.com/platform?e=e813143e1dc0d3b0ffcb007ffe357333&utm_source=jillsteinforpresident&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=scotus_rulings&n=4)** by expanding the court, pursuing term limits, and imposing a judicial code of ethics with a clear path to remove justices who abuse their power.

We can bring that plan to life when we win the White House and deliver a mandate for people, planet, and peace – restoring faith and confidence in our federal government in the process.

**[But I can’t do this alone. I need your support today to make sure we can pay our incredible team and reach the millions of voters who are looking for alternatives after the disastrous debate between the ruling parties Thursday night.](https://www.jillstein2024.com/donate?e=e813143e1dc0d3b0ffcb007ffe357333&utm_source=jillsteinforpresident&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=scotus_rulings&n=5)**

In solidarity and gratitude,

Jill

body:
We don’t have to live with this status quo
#

Friend -
There’s no doubt that we’re at an inflection point in our movement. Earlier this month, we experienced an immense setback after the Supreme Court struck down the ATF’s bump stock ban. Then just this week, we welcomed the news of Surgeon General Vivek Murthy having the courage to call our nation’s gun violence problem what it truly is: a public health crisis.
We’re making progress, but our opponents are fighting to erase it. Meanwhile, our gun violence crisis rages on.
We never should have gotten to this point.
We never should have gotten to the point where every day, over 120 people in our nation die from gun violence.
We never should have gotten to the point where nearly 44,000 people die from gun violence every year.
We never should have gotten to the point where gun violence has become the NUMBER ONE cause of death for children in our nation.
This is the status quo. But it doesn’t have to be this way. There are real solutions—such as universal background checks, safe storage laws, and extreme risk protection orders—that can help prevent gun violence and keep our communities safer.

**_WFP MAKES AN IMPACT IN NEW YORK RACES_**
While AIPAC may have succeeded in taking out one of our progressive champions in Congress, we were still able to grow our ranks of WFP electeds up and down the state. On Tuesday, we powered three progressive women of color to victory in their State Assembly races, took out a corrupt District Attorney, and protected every one of our state-level champions. Of the 27 WFP-endorsed candidates who had primary challenges — **19 won their elections.** Here are a few highlights from Tuesday night:
* **Gabriella Romero** won a six-way race to represent her Albany community in the State Assembly. A public defender and Common Councilmember, Gabriella will make sure that the voices of working people are heard in the halls of power.
* **Claire Valdez** won resoundingly in her Queens Assembly race. A proud UAW member, Claire will be a powerful champion for workers’ rights and climate protections in the legislature.
* **Lee Kindlon** defeated a scandal-ridden, twenty-year incumbent for Albany County District Attorney. We look forward to Lee bridging the gap between the DA’s office and the Albany community.

clean_body: Keep reading for updates on important upcoming primary elections, legislation, and how you can help. | | | Peter, It’s time for the WFP monthly newsletter, where we catch you up on the state of our movement and how we’re fighting — and winning — together. Keep reading for updates on important upcoming primary elections, legislation, and how you can help. JAMAAL BOWMAN LOSES PRIMARY TO AIPAC-BACKED GEORGE LATIMER AIPAC and other right-wing super PACs spent to oust Rep. Jamaal Bowman from his NY-16 House seat and elect their recruited candidate, Westchester County Executive George Latimer. Despite a powerful, multi-racial coalition coming together in defense of Rep. Jamaal Bowman, that kind of onslaught of spending was simply too much to overcome. AIPAC turned this race into the most expensive House primary in U.S. history, and their millions pushed their hand-picked candidate to the top in a race that came down to turnout. Still, we are incredibly proud of the effort our WFP team and members put together, and we are ready to continue the fight to make sure that we the people decide our representatives, not Republican billionaires. AIPAC’s next target is Rep. Cori Bush, who’s already facing millions in attack ads from some of the same dark-money Super PACs that came after Rep. Jamaal Bowman. We can’t let them win again, Peter. WFP MAKES AN IMPACT IN NEW YORK RACES While AIPAC may have succeeded in taking out one of our progressive champions in Congress, we were still able to grow our ranks of WFP electeds up and down the state. On Tuesday, we powered three progressive women of color to victory in their State Assembly races, took out a corrupt District Attorney, and protected every one of our state-level champions. Of the 27 WFP-endorsed candidates who had primary challenges — 19 won their elections. Here are a few highlights from Tuesday night: Gabriella Romero won a six-way race to represent her Albany community in the State Assembly. A public defender and Common Councilmember, Gabriella will make sure that the voices of working people are heard in the halls of power. Claire Valdez won resoundingly in her Queens Assembly race. A proud UAW member, Claire will be a powerful champion for workers’ rights and climate protections in the legislature. Lee Kindlon defeated a scandal-ridden, twenty-year incumbent for Albany County District Attorney. We look forward to Lee bridging the gap between the DA’s office and the Albany community. MORE VICTORIES IN NEW MEXICO, COLORADO PRIMARIES We celebrated a big primary night in New Mexico , where WFP won 89% of our races. Our movement defended every one of our incumbent champions, and helped bring new progressive leaders to victory and to governing power. Four Democratic state representatives who were blocking passage of paid family leave in the state lost to challengers we endorsed, a testament to the collective power of our movement, and the organizers who helped deliver this moment. For more coverage on how WFP and other progressives are continuing to reshape the state legislature in New Mexico, read the rundown by In Colorado , we saw several of our candidates overcome the bottomless pit of dark money that poured into their races. Colorado Working Families Party State Director Wendy Howell broke it down best: “The good news is that money surely couldn't buy them [corporate special interest groups] everything. While they certainly won a few races tonight, so did several of our community champions. In particular, Yara Zokaie in HD52 and Kathy Gebhardt for CD2 State Board of Education overcame huge corporate dark money spending against them to deliver powerful victories for our communities and our schools. And, in the race for SD28, which will likely go down as the most expensive state legislative primary in Colorado history with all of its corporate spending, community champion Rep. Mike Weissman appears to have won.” “We've known all along that we won't win every race we fight against the wealthy few - they've been buying our political system for years, so we know what they're capable of.But tonight we proved that they won't win every race either, no matter how much they spend. For our part, we plan to just keep fighting to elect community champions, all up and down Colorado's ballot, this fall and in the years to come — no matter how much corporate spending may come against us.” All in all, despite the record-breaking corporate spending stacked against us, our movement showed that the grassroots power of the many can take on dark money, and win. WFP’S CEASEFIRE PHONE BANK SHUTS DOWN THE WHITE HOUSE SWITCHBOARD Earlier this month, following the Israeli military's invasion of Rafah — one of the last places of refuge for Palestinians in war-stricken Gaza — we mobilized hundreds of WFP members across the country to contact voters and patch through calls to the White House demanding that President Biden honor his own red line and cease military funding and weapons shipments to the Israeli military. And the White House switchboard ended up the flood of calls. Collective action always makes a message clear, Charles. THE PENNSYLVANIA WORKING FAMILIES PARTY SECURES MAJOR VICTORIES In Philadelphia , the city council voted to make WFP Councilmember Kendra Brooks’ nationally-renowned Eviction Diversion Program permanent — a huge victory that will help keep tens of thousands of working people in their homes each year. Now, we’re launching an effort to strengthen this program and enact new legislation that invests $50 million in rental assistance to help tenants struggling to make ends meet to cover rent, utilities and other housing related expenses. For coverage, see Meanwhile, earlier this month, WFP National Director Maurice Mitchell joined hundreds of Pennsylvanians from across the state, including WFP councilmembers Kendra Brooks, Nicolas O’Rourke, and other allies, to demand that legislators deliver a historic increase in state funding for Pennsylvania’s public schools — and reject the expansion of private school voucher programs that only benefit the wealthy. The bill to increase funding by the billions for Pennsylvania’s public schools passed the House that night, thanks in part to the efforts led by PA WFP and a people-powered coalition of labor unions, deeply-rooted community organizations, and elected officials. It now moves to the Senate for a final vote. UPCOMING EVENTS: Over the last few months we've made over 250,000 calls to protect the Squad and now we're showing our power in St. Louis. With Rep. Cori Bush’s primary in Missouri just over two months away, WFP volunteers across the country are gathering for a phone bank, where we’ll reach voters about this crucial race. Join the call at 6:00 PM ET/3:00 PM PT this upcoming Monday, July 1st! Never made calls before? Don't worry, you'll get all of the training you need to call with confidence. We’ll walk you through how to make effective calls, and our organizers will be around to answer any questions. All you need is a computer or internet-connected device and a phone. On Thursday, July 25th at 7:00 PM ET/4:00 PM PT, join us for our monthly Welcome Gathering! These monthly calls are your opportunity — whether you’re new to the WFP or a long-time supporter — to hear directly from our staff and activists about the country and the party we’re building together. Join us on August 14th at 8:00 PM EST/ 5:00 PM PST for our third in a series of mass calls aimed at driving out hopelessness by grounding us in clarity and our power. We invite you to take a step back and examine with us the electoral chessboard, what opportunities we’ve successfully seized, and where we need to go next. With less than five months until Election Day nationwide, it’s crucial that we remain grounded in community, hope, clarity, and our movement’s power — and we’re hoping that through this series of mass calls, we’ll provide a space that continues to inspire us in these times of intense struggle. Thanks for making it to the end of our WFP newsletter, Peter! Hey, Peter-- If you're like me, you're getting lots of texts or calls from folks about the state of the race after Thursday. Maybe it was your panicked aunt, your MAGA uncle, or some self-important Podcasters. It's a tough position to be in, so I thought it might be helpful to send you a few responses.
1. **Yes, the debate started rough, but voters saw what a threat Donald Trump is to the country.** It was more than just lying -- though he did plenty of that. Trump:

* Defended the end of _Roe v. Wade_ , saying "it's been a great thing."
* Said that the pro-Trump Nazi march in Charlottesville was "made up."
* Said on January 6th that "we were respected all over the world."
* Defended his 34 felony convictions, saying the system was "rigged" and he did nothing wrong.
2. **Actual voters perceived this debate very differently than those who pay attention to politics a lot (like everyone who is getting this email and everyone who goes on cable news).**
Breaking news: People think Joe Biden's old. They did coming into the debate, they do coming out of the debate. At the same time, though, a lot of people have rose-colored glasses about the Trump years. The most important thing about the debate was always going to be that people were reminded of what they hate about Donald Trump: that he's unhinged, out for revenge, and in it for himself. And they were reminded, in a powerful way.

clean_body: | | | Hey, Peter-- If you're like me, you're getting lots of texts or calls from folks about the state of the race after Thursday. Maybe it was your panicked aunt, your MAGA uncle, or some self-important Podcasters. It's a tough position to be in, so I thought it might be helpful to send you a few responses. 1. Yes, the debate started rough, but voters saw what a threat Donald Trump is to the country. It was more than just lying -- though he did plenty of that. Trump: Defended the end of Roe v. Wade , saying "it's been a great thing." Said that the pro-Trump Nazi march in Charlottesville was "made up." Said on January 6th that "we were respected all over the world." Defended his 34 felony convictions, saying the system was "rigged" and he did nothing wrong. 2. Actual voters perceived this debate very differently than those who pay attention to politics a lot (like everyone who is getting this email and everyone who goes on cable news). Breaking news: People think Joe Biden's old. They did coming into the debate, they do coming out of the debate. At the same time, though, a lot of people have rose-colored glasses about the Trump years. The most important thing about the debate was always going to be that people were reminded of what they hate about Donald Trump: that he's unhinged, out for revenge, and in it for himself. And they were reminded, in a powerful way. Flash polls from , , , , and show what we expected: the debate did not change the horserace. In fact, following the debate, our internal dials showed President Biden led Trump on key measures of being presidential, speaking to the issues that matter, and being likable by more than 20 points. 3. That's because the long-term impact of debates is overstated anyway. Let us all remember that Barack Obama lost the first debate in 2012 (and the media panicked too!). Bush lost in 2004. Ronald Reagan lost the first debate in 1984. They, as you'll recall, won their elections. And those debates were in October, not June! 4. 90 minutes does not negate 3 1⁄2 years of results. Joe Biden is extremely good at being president. Let's not forget that the guy up on stage: Expanded health care to millions of families Lowered the price of insulin to $35 for seniors Created more jobs than any president in history Vaccinated the country and reopened our schools Took the largest climate action in the history of the world Canceled student loans for nearly 5 million people Rallied the world in support of Ukraine, and expanded NATO while doing it Passed the largest national funding for passenger rail since the founding of Amtrak Banned chokeholds and no-knock entries by federal law enforcement, and restricted the transfer of military equipment to police departments Passed the largest investment in bridges and roads in our history Pardoned thousands of Americans federally convicted of marijuana possession Expanded benefits to veterans who have been exposed to toxic chemicals Officially protected same-sex marriage federally Passed the first gun violence prevention bill in 30 years Saved the pensions of more than 1 million union workers Averted a banking crisis (remember that?) Expanded paid overtime to working families Made birth control pills available over the counter Made renewable energy the #2 source of electricity in America Moved to reschedule marijuana Shifted the microchip supply chain back to the United States Put the first Black woman on the Supreme Court And that's really all I have time to list out here! 5. The day after the debate, Joe Biden gave a fiery, defiant speech, where he tackled concerns about his age head-on. I don't know if you were watching, but Joe Biden left the debate stage, spoke at a rally, , got on a plane, flew to Raleigh, hung out with 200 supporters on the tarmac, went to bed, woke up, gave an amazing speech, got back on a plane, went to New York, visited Stonewall with Elton John, and then spoke at a pride gala for LGBTQ+ supporters. The speech in Raleigh, by the way, has millions of views online, and you should yourself: 6. The bedwetting brigade is calling for Joe Biden to "drop out." That is the best possible way for Donald Trump to win and us to lose. First of all: Joe Biden is going to be the Democratic nominee, period. End of story. Voters voted. He won overwhelmingly. And if he were to drop out, it would lead to weeks of chaos, internal foodfighting, and a bunch of candidates who limp into a brutal floor fight at the convention, all while Donald Trump has time to speak to American voters uncontested. All of that would be in service of a nominee who would go into a general election in the weakest possible position with zero dollars in their bank account. You want a highway to losing? It's that. And at the end of the day, we'd switch to candidates who would, according to polls, be less likely to win than Joe Biden -- the only person ever to defeat Donald Trump. 7. Joe Biden is the Democratic nominee, period. Rather than worrying about polls, our supporters are getting on board. Did you see the awesome clips of our supporters on the tarmac doing the Cupid Shuffle at 2am on the night of the debate? The biggest rally of our campaign yet on Friday? Well, no, probably not, because the media is busy hyperventilating and trying to manifest drama to boost ratings. But this isn't Aaron Sorkin's fever dream. It's Joe Biden's reelection campaign. While they were spinning out, our grassroots supporters got to work and: Raised us $27 million in two days Signed up for three times as many volunteer shifts as on an average day Attended more than 1,500 events nationwide We even had three times as many people as usual apply to campaign jobs yesterday. Mercifully, while the beltway pundits are spending their time attacking Joe Biden, our people are more focused than ever. Smart folks -- folks that care about defeating Donald Trump and winning this election -- have identified that the best way to help right now is by helping, and not by kicking their feet up and telling everyone around them to panic. This brings me to what you can do right now. 1. Donate to our campaign. Seriously, it makes a difference. Of that $27 million, the vast vast majority comes from $5, $10, $25 donations. We are a campaign of grassroots supporters -- and we need you now more than ever. | | | 2. Share why you support the President on social media. The internet is not real life, but your friends really are. Every social media post supporting the President reaches real voters, and also helps us counteract the negative narrative around the President. You don't need to do anything fancy to post, but if you want to let us know how it went, : | | 3. Sign up for a volunteer shift. Talking to voters is more important than fretting about polls. There's an organizer in your neighborhood who would love to talk to you. | | 4. Forward this email to someone who you think needs to see it. And tell them to . And lastly, but most importantly, you've got to keep the faith. I've worked for Joe Biden for five years, which is a pretty short tenure comparatively. I've watched as people counted him out after Iowa in 2020, and then he won. I've watched as they said there was no way he could win the general election (do not think I have forgotten the week of New York Times opinion pieces about how Joe Biden needed to change his campaign strategy), and then he won. I've watched as people said his legislative agenda was dead, and then he passed the Inflation Reduction Act. I've watched as people said he'd get cooked in the midterms, and then Democrats had historic wins. There is no candidate who is better when he's backed into a corner, and there is no team that is better when we come together to do big things. That's because we, like him, keep our heads down and do the work. As the President says, when you get knocked down, you get back up again. And as some poets once said: you're never going to keep him down. Thanks for being in this with us. Rob Flaherty Deputy Campaign Manager Biden for President

body:
# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=1601%2E135344%2E4l8MYL)

Friends --
June 30th marks the second FEC deadline of the year and that means if you're anything like us, your inbox is filled with requests from political campaigns and organizations asking for donations.
With your permission, I’d appreciate the chance to make the case for why a donation to my campaign for U.S. Senate is one of the most strategic contributions you can make on Sunday.
Let me start with what you probably already instinctively know: Michigan is going to be a critical state for the 2024 campaign.
There is no winning the White House without Michigan. For Democrats, there is no holding the Senate without Michigan. Even our House delegation rests on a one-seat Democratic majority.
But you were probably already sold on the importance of Michigan. So, aside from the fact that control of the U.S. Senate is at stake (!), what about my race? Why donate to my campaign?
This is one of the rare open Senate races without an incumbent running -- in fact, it’s one of the few competitive races in the entire country. That means we have A LOT of introducing of me to do across the state. A recent poll showed about 50% of the state knows me, across our 11 media markets.
Reaching those folks takes resources, and that's not something I can do without you.
Add the fact that this is going to be one of the most expensive races in the country -- not just with candidate spending, but outside spending too.
And I'll close with the news that in all of my elections, I have historically done better than Democrats usually do in the "redder" areas of the state. That means I am finding and pulling voters other races couldn't, and that is good for everyone up and down the ballot on Election Day.
So yes, this race is kind of a unicorn. It's a unique situation where control of the White House and Congress is on the line, most voters don't know the candidates yet, and the Democratic Senate candidate can help the top of the ticket, and not the other way around.
[**That's why I am asking for your support: Can I count on you to make a contribution to my campaign for U.S. Senate before our FEC fundraising drive ends tomorrow? I would not ask if it were not so important.](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-june24.nyVfY7&refcode=em240629-3&t=2&akid=1601%2E135344%2E4l8MYL)**
